Evidence
  • 156 boards were above the upper limit, all built between 02:00 and 02:40 (peak 257.9–259.8 °C, spec 245–255 °C).
  • 44 of the 47 bridged boards were built in that window.
  • Outside the window, peak reflow averaged 251.8 °C and only 3 boards bridged.
How this was calculated
stg-B0003 boardsSolder bridgingNo defectDefect rate
Above USL4411228.2%
In spec32,4010.125%
226× = 28.2% ÷ 0.125%. The causal path comes from the Failure Library rule PeakReflowTemperature > USL → ExcessReflowSpreading.
Out-of-spec boards were 6.1% of the batch (156 of 2,560) but had 94% of the bridges (44 of 47).
Fisher's exact test: p < 0.001. The gap between 28.2% and 0.125% is far too large to be random variation.
Suggested action: Lock the approved reflow recipe and confirm how a different profile was loaded at 02:00.

How a cause is linked

A root cause is linked when its parameter was out of spec in this batch and all three hold:
  • the defect is at least 2× more likely on out-of-spec boards
  • the gap is too large to be random variation (Fisher's exact test, p < 0.01)
  • it explains at least 20% of the defective boards
